l4_steps.name: Monitor CBA amendable date and trigger opening
l4_steps.input: Current CBA contract dates, calendar alert at 180-day threshold
l4_steps.output: Opening trigger memo; formal Section 6 notice preparation initiated
l4_steps.kpi: Opening notice filed ≥180 days before CBA amendable date; 100% of contracts tracked in SuccessFactors
l4_steps.pain_point: Under the Railway Labour Act (RLA), contracts do not expire — they become 'amendable'; status quo obligation means outdated terms can persist indefinitely if airline fails to file timely, freezing modernisation of scheduling systems and work rules

l4_steps.name: Benchmark labour costs against peer carriers
l4_steps.input: Current pay scales from SAP SuccessFactors; DOT Form 41 peer carrier filings; IATA airline cost data
l4_steps.output: Labour cost benchmarking report (cost gap vs. Delta, United, American, Southwest)
l4_steps.kpi: Data currency ≤90 days old; peer set covers ≥5 major carriers; report delivered ≥150 days before amendable date
l4_steps.pain_point: DOT Form 41 labour cost data is lagged 6–12 months; actual competitor total compensation packages (profit sharing, equity, per diem) are often not disclosed until SEC filings or union leaks, skewing benchmark modelling

l4_steps.name: Model financial impact of proposed contract changes
l4_steps.input: Benchmarking report; current headcount, pay grades, and FTE data from SAP SuccessFactors
l4_steps.output: Financial impact model with ≥5 pay scenarios, NPV over contract term, and cost-per-ASM sensitivity analysis
l4_steps.kpi: Model covers ≥5 scenarios; labour cost projection accuracy within ±2% of actuals at year-end; model delivered 120 days before amendable date
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-year contract costing requires fuel price and ASM growth assumptions that are highly uncertain; modelling errors >5% have triggered mid-contract re-opening demands and resulted in $100M+ unbudgeted labour cost overruns at major US carriers

l4_steps.name: Form cross-functional management negotiating team
l4_steps.role: Chief People Officer / VP Labour Relations
l4_steps.input: Board/CEO negotiation parameters; legal counsel engagement; financial model from Step 1.3
l4_steps.output: Negotiation team charter; defined mandate authority limits; war-room SharePoint site stood up
l4_steps.kpi: Team constituted ≥120 days before target opening session; team includes Legal, Finance, Operations, and HR representation
l4_steps.pain_point: Conflicting priorities between Operations (scheduling flexibility), Finance (cost ceiling), and HR (retention) create an incoherent management position; union negotiators routinely exploit internal inconsistencies to extract additional concessions worth 1–3% of contract value

l4_steps.name: Develop management opening proposals and costing
l4_steps.input: Benchmarking report; financial model; operational requirements from Flight Operations and Crew Planning
l4_steps.output: Management opening proposal document with article-by-article positions; cost envelope per article
l4_steps.kpi: Proposal reviewed by outside labour counsel within 10 business days; FAR Part 117 and ICAO fatigue regulation compliance verified for all scheduling provisions
l4_steps.pain_point: Airline ops constraints (FAR Part 117 rest rules, ICAO fatigue regulations, irregular operations pay) must be precisely reflected in scheduling and duty-time contract language; ambiguous drafting creates compliance liability and exposes carrier to FAA enforcement action

l4_steps.name: Obtain board approval of negotiation mandate
l4_steps.input: Draft opening proposal; financial model with cost ceiling; outside counsel legal review sign-off
l4_steps.output: Board-approved negotiation mandate with cost ceiling and fall-back positions
l4_steps.kpi: Mandate approved before first bargaining session; cost ceiling grounded in verified FI/CO labour cost baseline
l4_steps.pain_point: Boards often set unrealistic cost ceilings based on prior-cycle assumptions or competitor announcements rather than current market data; mid-negotiation mandate revisions require additional board sessions, causing 3–6 month delays and signalling weakness to union

l4_steps.name: File Section 6 notice and open formal bargaining
l4_steps.input: Board-approved management proposal; union's Section 6 notice received
l4_steps.output: Bargaining docket opened in NMB portal; first session date confirmed; ground rules agreed
l4_steps.kpi: First bargaining session convened within 30 days of mutual Section 6 notice exchange
l4_steps.pain_point: Under the RLA status quo obligation, the airline cannot unilaterally change rates, rules, or working conditions during negotiations — a perpetual obligation that incentivises union delay tactics, with some RLA negotiations running 5–10 years before resolution

l4_steps.name: Conduct iterative proposal exchange and counter-proposals
l4_steps.role: Labour Relations Manager / Union Bargaining Committee
l4_steps.input: Opening proposals from both parties; session minutes; ground rules agreement
l4_steps.output: Redlined contract drafts per session; session tracker; consolidated open items log
l4_steps.kpi: Open items log reduced by ≥10% per bargaining month; no previously agreed article reopened without written consent of both parties
l4_steps.pain_point: Aviation-specific provisions (deadhead travel standards, hotel quality tiers, irregular operation pay triggers, open-time bidding rules) generate 60–80 contested articles that resist quick resolution; pattern bargaining pressures from other carriers complicate single-carrier negotiations

l4_steps.name: Track tentative agreements and maintain open issues log
l4_steps.input: Session minutes; articles agreed (TA) and disputed articles from each bargaining session
l4_steps.output: TA log (articles agreed with effective dates); open issues register with union and management positions per article
l4_steps.kpi: TA log updated within 24 hours of each session; open issues register shared with both parties within 48 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Without a structured tracker, previously agreed articles get reopened through 'linked bargaining' tactics, extending negotiations by 3–6 months; several major US airline negotiations have collapsed at the TA stage due to tracking failures

l4_steps.name: Assess bargaining progress and declare impasse if warranted
l4_steps.input: Open issues register; session count; timeline vs. target; financial model thresholds
l4_steps.output: Impasse declaration to NMB, or continued bargaining directive with revised target milestones
l4_steps.kpi: ≥75% of articles TA'd before NMB referral; target contract duration ≤24 months from opening notice to ratification
l4_steps.pain_point: The 2022–2024 US pilot shortage dramatically increased union leverage, extending pilot contract negotiations by 18+ months beyond historical norms; airlines that delayed impasse declarations lost scheduling certainty during peak summer hiring and capacity planning cycles

l4_steps.name: Request NMB mediation and establish case docket
l4_steps.input: Impasse declaration; unresolved articles list with positions documented
l4_steps.output: NMB case docket opened; assigned mediator confirmed; first mediated session scheduled
l4_steps.kpi: NMB application filed within 5 business days of impasse declaration; first mediated session convened within 45 days of NMB acceptance
l4_steps.pain_point: NMB mediation under the RLA is open-ended with no statutory time limit; airlines have been in NMB mediation for 3–7 years, making 5-year fleet planning, pilot hiring targets, and network capacity decisions highly uncertain throughout

l4_steps.name: Conduct NMB-mediated bargaining and resolve open articles
l4_steps.role: VP Labour Relations / NMB Mediator / Union President
l4_steps.input: NMB mediator briefing package; remaining open articles; financial parameters
l4_steps.output: Additional TAs on mediated articles; mediator recommendations; or NMB proffer of arbitration if impasse persists
l4_steps.kpi: Open articles reduced by ≥50% within 90 days of mediation start; full TA reached before proffer of arbitration where possible
l4_steps.pain_point: NMB proffer of arbitration triggers a mandatory 30-day cooling-off period after which 'self-help' (strikes, lockouts, unilateral change) becomes legal — the resulting operational and reputational risk has cost airlines $500M–$2B in market cap losses within 48 hours of strike announcements

l4_steps.name: Draft and execute full tentative agreement
l4_steps.role: Labour Relations Manager / Legal Counsel / Union Bargaining Committee
l4_steps.input: All TAs from bargaining and mediation sessions; mediator-brokered language; financial model final scenario
l4_steps.output: Fully executed tentative agreement document (all articles); implementation date schedule
l4_steps.kpi: Legal review completed within 15 business days; zero unresolved ambiguous provisions; implementation timeline agreed before union ratification vote
l4_steps.pain_point: Ambiguous contract language in scheduling system provisions (e.g. how crew management software generates open-time offers, or how irregular ops pay is calculated from ACARS data) becomes the primary source of grievances within 90 days of implementation, driving arbitration costs

l4_steps.name: Conduct union membership ratification vote
l4_steps.input: Signed TA; union member roster from SAP SuccessFactors; voting eligibility rules
l4_steps.output: Ratification vote result (pass/fail with percentage); formal ratification notice to management
l4_steps.kpi: Voter turnout ≥60%; ratification threshold >50% of votes cast per union bylaws; result certified within 5 business days of vote close
l4_steps.pain_point: Failed ratification votes (e.g. American Airlines pilot TA rejected in 2023 requiring renegotiation) delay implementation by 6–18 months, trigger stock price decline of 3–8%, and force management back to bargaining with a weakened position and increased union expectations

l4_steps.name: Implement ratified agreement in HR and payroll systems
l4_steps.input: Ratified agreement with effective dates; retroactive pay calculation if amendable date predates ratification
l4_steps.output: Updated pay scales, work rules, and benefits configurations in SuccessFactors; payroll cutover completed; retro pay processed
l4_steps.kpi: All pay changes live within 30 days of ratification; retroactive pay (if applicable) paid within 60 days; payroll error rate <0.1% of affected employees
l4_steps.pain_point: Complex retroactive pay calculations (back pay owed from amendable date, potentially 1–4 years prior, to thousands of employees) require manual reconciliation when SAP SuccessFactors lacks a native retro-pay engine for custom union pay scales, creating $10M+ reconciliation risk

l4_steps.name: Distribute contract and conduct manager training
l4_steps.role: Labour Relations Manager / HR Business Partners
l4_steps.input: Final executed contract; implementation guidelines; manager briefing deck
l4_steps.output: Contract published to employee self-service portal; manager training completion records in SAP SuccessFactors LMS
l4_steps.kpi: Contract accessible to 100% of covered employees within 14 days of ratification; ≥90% of frontline managers trained within 30 days; training completion tracked in SuccessFactors LMS
l4_steps.pain_point: Inconsistent manager interpretation of new scheduling provisions and irregular ops pay rules is the primary source of early grievances post-ratification; structured manager briefing has been shown to reduce first-year grievance rate by ~30% at comparable carriers

l4_steps.name: Monitor grievance filings and manage compliance
l4_steps.role: Labour Relations Coordinator / HR Business Partners
l4_steps.input: Employee or union grievance filings; relevant contract provisions; prior arbitration precedents
l4_steps.output: Grievance case log; Step 1/2/3 resolution decisions; arbitration referrals with legal brief
l4_steps.kpi: Step 1 grievance response within 10 business days; ≥70% of grievances resolved at Step 1 or 2 without arbitration; arbitration spend <$500K per year per contract group
l4_steps.pain_point: Accumulation of unresolved grievances — particularly around scheduling systems and irregular ops — creates a poisoned industrial relations climate entering the next contract cycle, amplifying union leverage; airlines with >500 open grievances at amendable date face 15–25% higher settlement premiums
